subdomain: 2.5 Implement prompt reuse strategies (caching, modular prompts, Skills)

en.question: A service caches its unchanged system instructions, but required customer-specific tool schemas differ in the top-level tools array. The service must keep those schemas distinct and does not use an inline tool-change feature. The team expects one system cache entry to be reusable across all customers because the system text is identical. Which adjustment follows the documented prefix hierarchy?

options.text: Extend the system entry's lifetime and share it across customer schemas, treating longer retention as permission to ignore preceding tools.
options.note: Lifetime does not alter the prefix hash. The system cache depends on the earlier tools portion as well as the system text.

options.text: Group reuse measurements by identical tools-and-system prefixes, retaining distinct required schemas and accounting for separate writes.
options.note: The cache hierarchy is tools, then system, then messages. Different top-level tools create different cumulative system prefixes even when system text is unchanged.

options.text: Serialize system before tools in the request JSON so that the system cache no longer depends on the tools.
options.note: Object-key order in the request does not replace the documented cache hierarchy. The effective prefix still includes tools before system content.

options.text: Mark an earlier system block and expect it to match independently of the tools array.
options.note: Moving within the system section can exclude later system text but cannot exclude the preceding tools. It does not create a tool-independent system prefix.
